questions.question: List the basic components of a function definition.
questions.solution_html:
• List the basic components of a function definition.
  • The basic components are the def keyword, function name, parentheses, optional parameters
  • colon and function body. A return statement may also be included.
  • ImportError: Occurs when an imported module cannot be loaded.
  • Exception Handling in Python
  • Exception handling is a method of handling runtime errors so that the program can continue or terminate
  • gracefully instead of stopping unexpectedly.
  • Python uses the following keywords for exception handling
  •  try: Contains the code that may produce an exception.
  •  except: Handles the exception.
  •  else: Executes if no exception occurs in the try block.
  •  finally: Executes whether an exception occurs or not.
  •  raise: Used to generate an exception manually.
  • Example program
  • try
  • a = int(input("Enter a number: "))
  • b = int(input("Enter another number: "))
  • result = a / b
  • print("Result:", result)
  • except ZeroDivisionError
  • print("Cannot divide by zero")
  • except ValueError
  • print("Please enter valid numbers")
  • finally
  • print("Program completed")
  • Defining a New Exception in Python
  • Python allows programmers to define their own exceptions by creating a class derived from the built-in
  • Exception class. These are called user-defined exceptions. The raise keyword is used to generate the custom
  • exception.
  • Example program
  • class AgeError(Exception)
  • pass
  • age = int(input("Enter your age: "))
  • try
  • if age < 18
  • raise AgeError("Age must be 18 or above")
  • print("Eligible to vote")
  • except AgeError as e
  • print(e)
questions.final_answer: print(e)

questions.question: Outline the client-server model used in socket programming
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the client-server model used in socket programming.
  • The client-server model is a communication model in which a client requests a service and a server
  • provides the service. Python socket programming allows applications to communicate over a network. A
  • socket acts as an endpoint for communication.In TCP socket programming, the server creates a socket and
  • binds it to an IP address and port number. It listens for connection requests and accepts a client
  • connection. The client creates its own socket and connects to the server. After establishing the connection
  • they exchange data and close the connection when communication is complete.
  • Basic flow
  • Example: A web browser acts as a client when it requests a webpage from a web server. The server
  • processes the request and sends the webpage data back to the browser.
questions.final_answer: processes the request and sends the webpage data back to the browser

questions.question: Discuss sets in Python and explain their creation, properties, and / common operations.
questions.solution_html:
• A set in Python is an unordered collection of unique elements. It does not allow duplicate values
  • and is useful for performing mathematical set operations.
  • Creation of a Set
  • A set is created using curly braces {} or the set() function.
  • A = {10, 20, 30, 40}
  • B = {30, 40, 50, 60}
  • Properties of Sets:Sets contain only unique elements, Sets are unordered collections, Elements
  • can be added or removed,Sets do not support indexing.
  • Common Set Operations: - Union (|): Combines elements from both sets, Intersection (&)
  • Returns common elements.Difference (-): Returns elements present in the first set but not the second.
  • Symmetric difference (^): Returns elements present in either set, but not in both.
  • A = {10, 20, 30, 40}
  • B = {30, 40, 50, 60}
  • print("Union:", A | B)
  • print("Intersection:", A & B)
  • print("Difference:", A - B)
  • print("Symmetric Difference:", A ^ B)
questions.final_answer: Option B)

questions.question: Outline the client-server model used in socket programming
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the client-server model used in socket programming.
  • The client-server model is a communication model in which a client requests a service and a server
  • provides the service. Python socket programming allows applications to communicate over a network. A
  • socket acts as an endpoint for communication.In TCP socket programming, the server creates a socket and
  • binds it to an IP address and port number. It listens for connection requests and accepts a client
  • connection. The client creates its own socket and connects to the server. After establishing the connection
  • they exchange data and close the connection when communication is complete.
  • Basic flow
  • Example: A web browser acts as a client when it requests a webpage from a web server. The server
  • processes the request and sends the webpage data back to the browser.
questions.final_answer: processes the request and sends the webpage data back to the browser

questions.question: Discuss sets in Python and explain their creation, properties, and / common operations.
questions.solution_html:
• A set in Python is an unordered collection of unique elements. It does not allow duplicate values
  • and is useful for performing mathematical set operations.
  • Creation of a Set
  • A set is created using curly braces {} or the set() function.
  • A = {10, 20, 30, 40}
  • B = {30, 40, 50, 60}
  • Properties of Sets:Sets contain only unique elements, Sets are unordered collections, Elements
  • can be added or removed,Sets do not support indexing.
  • Common Set Operations: - Union (|): Combines elements from both sets, Intersection (&)
  • Returns common elements.Difference (-): Returns elements present in the first set but not the second.
  • Symmetric difference (^): Returns elements present in either set, but not in both.
  • A = {10, 20, 30, 40}
  • B = {30, 40, 50, 60}
  • print("Union:", A | B)
  • print("Intersection:", A & B)
  • print("Difference:", A - B)
  • print("Symmetric Difference:", A ^ B)
questions.final_answer: Option B)
